overview: The MPS Strategic & Capital Planning subcommittee oversees the district's long-term strategy, multi-year capital improvements, facility allocations, and policy development. Its work spans from May 2021 through May 2026 across several school committee terms. Key responsibilities include creating facility naming and capital planning frameworks, prioritizing urgent infrastructure projects, managing elementary school overcrowding, and designing community visioning processes. At its most recent meeting, the body set a timeline targeting February 2027 for a finalized strategic plan and pursued grant funding for a technical consultant.

threads.name: District Strategic Planning
threads.summary: The subcommittee initially reviewed an updated draft District Strategy for Improvement in May 2021 and voted to forward it to the full School Committee. In October 2025, the body launched a multi-phase community engagement process involving public surveys and focus groups to redefine district priorities and mission statements. By May 2026, the subcommittee established a schedule targeting a finalized strategic plan by February 2027. It also moved to coordinate strategic visioning with facility studies and pursue grant funding for consultant assistance.

threads.name: Capital Planning Framework and Priorities
threads.summary: The subcommittee re-established an annual capital planning process in May 2024, approving a draft policy to restore district oversight of facility needs. Throughout late 2024, members categorized building maintenance and security projects into prioritized lists to align with municipal budget cycles. In late 2025, the committee refined its project spreadsheet using facility assessment data and adapted its format to meet city requirements. The subcommittee continues to update and forward recommended capital plans to the full School Committee.

threads.name: School Infrastructure and Repairs
threads.summary: The subcommittee systematically tracks building maintenance and major infrastructure requirements across district facilities. In late 2024, members outlined municipal bonding packages for bundled HVAC and roof reconstruction projects while preparing applications for state repair programs. By late 2025, the Massachusetts School Building Authority approved statements of interest for roof and HVAC replacements at three elementary schools. The committee also maintains ongoing oversight over active security upgrades, elevator repairs, and cooling systems.

threads.name: Elementary Overcrowding and Space Management
threads.summary: In May 2025, the subcommittee reviewed enrollment and capacity data revealing severe space constraints at the Roberts Elementary School. To provide immediate relief, the committee voted to relocate preschool classrooms to Missituk School and requested additional staffing. The committee also voted to establish a strategic space planning task force to handle community engagement around space studies. By May 2026, the subcommittee aligned these facility space decisions with ongoing strategic planning and potential grade reconfigurations.

threads.name: Playground Development and Funding
threads.summary: The subcommittee evaluated fundraising and donor options for the McGlynn Elementary Playground, which reached 50 percent completion in May 2024. The committee subsequently focused on Roberts Elementary as a top priority for playground updates due to footprint constraints. By late 2025, the body sought Community Preservation Act funding to support design and feasibility studies for renovations across three remaining school playgrounds.

threads.name: School Facility Naming Policy
threads.summary: In February 2023, the subcommittee drafted a policy establishing procedures and authority for naming school buildings, grounds, and interior spaces. The draft policy included clarification supporting the recommendations of naming advisory committees. The subcommittee approved the policy and referred it to the full School Committee.
